# WrapPanel

Header: `winui/ui/panels/WrapPanel.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/panels/WrapPanel.hpp`.

A panel that places its children one after another along a line and starts a new line when the next child would cross the far edge. Use it for tag chips, a toolbar of variable-width buttons, or a gallery of cards that reflows with the window.

Along the orientation children sit [item_spacing()](#item_spacing) apart; lines sit [line_spacing()](#line_spacing) apart, each as tall as its tallest child, and every child in a line is arranged at the line's full height. The panel asks for its widest line by the sum of its lines, plus the padding. A first child wider than the whole panel does not push an empty line in front of itself. Built declaratively by [`ui::WrapPanel`](#uiwrappanel).

Example: 
```cpp
// Declarative:
window.set_content(ui::WrapPanel{
    .item_spacing = 8.0f,
    .line_spacing = 8.0f,
    .padding      = ui::Thickness{12.0f},
    .content      = {
        ui::Button{.text = "Alpha"},
        ui::Button{.text = "Beta"},
        ui::Button{.text = "A much longer gamma"},
        ui::Button{.text = "Delta"},
    },
});

// Imperative:
auto panel = std::make_unique<ui::WrapPanelControl>();
panel->set_orientation(ui::Orientation::Horizontal);
panel->set_item_spacing(8.0f);
panel->set_line_spacing(4.0f);
panel->set_items_stretch(ui::WrapPanelItemsStretch::Last);
for (const char* tag : {"red", "green", "blue", "cyan", "magenta"})
{
    panel->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>(tag));
}
window.set_content(std::move(panel));
```

## `ui::WrapPanel`

Children in lines that wrap. Builds a [ui::WrapPanelControl](#uiwrappanelcontrol).

Children keep their desired size; a line breaks when the next child would not fit.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Spec chip(const char* text) { return ui::Button{.text = text}; }

window.set_content(ui::WrapPanel{
    .item_spacing = 8,
    .line_spacing = 8,
    .padding      = ui::Thickness{12.0f},
    .content      = {chip("Alpha"), chip("Beta item"), chip("Gamma"), chip("Delta item")},
});
```

```cpp
ui::WrapPanel{
    .orientation, .item_spacing, .line_spacing, .items_stretch, .padding, .background,
    .border_brush, .border_thickness, .corner_radius, .style, .margin, .width, .height,
    .min_width, .min_height, .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment,
    .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip, .enabled, .accessibility, .on_pointer_entered,
    .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control,
    .content
}
```

### build

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<Element> build()&&
```

Consumes the spec and returns the built [ui::WrapPanelControl](#uiwrappanelcontrol); the caller owns it.

## `ui::WrapPanelControl`

Derives from `ui::Panel`.

A panel that places its children one after another along a line and starts a new line when the next child would cross the far edge. Use it for tag chips, a toolbar of variable-width buttons, or a gallery of cards that reflows with the window.

Along the orientation children sit [item_spacing()](#item_spacing) apart; lines sit [line_spacing()](#line_spacing) apart, each as tall as its tallest child, and every child in a line is arranged at the line's full height. The panel asks for its widest line by the sum of its lines, plus the padding. A first child wider than the whole panel does not push an empty line in front of itself. Built declaratively by [`ui::WrapPanel`](#uiwrappanel).

Example: 
```cpp
// Declarative:
window.set_content(ui::WrapPanel{
    .item_spacing = 8.0f,
    .line_spacing = 8.0f,

    panel->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>(tag));

window.set_content(std::move(panel));
```

### WrapPanelControl

```cpp
WrapPanelControl() = default
```

An empty horizontal panel with no spacing, no padding and no stretch.

### add

```cpp
template <typename T>
T* add(std::unique_ptr<T> child)
```

Appends `child`, taking ownership, and returns a non-owning observer to it. Children are placed in the order added.

### add

```cpp
template <SpecLike S>
Element* add(S&& spec)
```

The declarative overload: builds `spec` (or takes the node a [ui::Spec](../tree/spec-vocabulary.md#class-spec) holds) and adds it as [add()](#add) does a control. Returns the built node as an [Element](../tree/element.md), or nullptr for an empty [ui::Spec](../tree/spec-vocabulary.md#class-spec), which adds nothing; a spec's `.control` field gives a typed observer.

### orientation

```cpp
Orientation orientation() const
```

The flow direction: Horizontal (rows, the default) or Vertical (columns).

### set_orientation

```cpp
void set_orientation(Orientation orientation)
```

Changes the flow direction; invalidates layout.

```cpp
float item_spacing() const
```

```cpp
void set_item_spacing(float spacing)
```

### line_spacing

```cpp
float line_spacing() const
```

The gap between two lines, in DIPs. Default 0.

### set_line_spacing

```cpp
void set_line_spacing(float spacing)
```

Sets the gap between lines; invalidates layout.

### items_stretch

```cpp
WrapPanelItemsStretch items_stretch() const
```

Whether the last child is widened to the end of its line. Default None.

### set_items_stretch

```cpp
void set_items_stretch(WrapPanelItemsStretch stretch)
```

Sets whether the last child is widened; invalidates layout.

### parallel_measure_safe

```cpp
bool parallel_measure_safe() const override
```

True: measuring touches only the panel and its children.

### border_brush

```cpp
std::optional<Color> border_brush() const
```

The outline color; nullopt (the default) draws no border even with a non-zero [`border_thickness()`](#border_thickness). Nullopt as well while a [ThemeColor](../tree/theme-color.md) is set.

### border_brush_resource

```cpp
ThemeColor border_brush_resource() const
```

The theme resource the border is drawn from, or null.

### border_thickness

```cpp
const Thickness& border_thickness() const
```

The border width in DIPs per side (default zero); it insets the children like padding.

### corner_radius

```cpp
float corner_radius() const
```

The corner radius in DIPs, uniform for all four corners (default 0, square).

### padding

```cpp
const Thickness& padding() const
```

The padding in DIPs between the border and the children (default zero).

### set_border_brush

```cpp
void set_border_brush(std::optional<Color> color)
```

A fixed outline color; replaces any resource. Marks the panel for redraw.

### set_border_brush

```cpp
void set_border_brush(ThemeColor resource)
```

An outline color read from the theme each time the panel is drawn; replaces any fixed color. Marks the panel for redraw.

### set_border_thickness

```cpp
void set_border_thickness(const Thickness& thickness)
```

Sets the border width; marks the panel for layout and redraw.

### set_corner_radius

```cpp
void set_corner_radius(float radius)
```

Sets the corner radius; marks the panel for redraw.

### set_padding

```cpp
void set_padding(const Thickness& padding)
```

Sets the padding; marks the panel for layout.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Lays the children out in lines against `available` (less the padding) and returns the widest line by the sum of the lines, plus the padding.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Wraps against `final_rect`'s size and places each child in its slot, every child as tall as its line and the last one stretched when [items_stretch()](#items_stretch) is Last.

## Enumerations

### WrapPanelItemsStretch

```cpp
enum class WrapPanelItemsStretch
```

Whether a [WrapPanel](#uiwrappanel) stretches its last child.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `None` | every child keeps its desired length along the line (the default) |
| `Last` | the panel's last child is widened to the end of its line |
